final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest LOF-proxy score in the probed set (AlphaMissense 0.991) with near-zero ESM-1v plausibility; replacing a buried, conserved tryptophan with arginine in the linker/regulatory core should destabilize the fold and abolish catalysis.

Position 227 is verified Thr and shows severe intolerance (T227I AlphaMissense 0.966, ESM-1v ≈0); T227M is additionally a documented severe MTHFR-deficiency allele, making near-null activity highly likely.
AlphaMissense 0.947 and ESM-1v 0.000 at a conserved Cys-Cys motif of the FAD-binding catalytic barrel; burying a charged arginine there should disrupt cofactor binding and eliminate activity.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence from the pathogenicity/LOF proxy and PLM tools is already saturated and mutually consistent for the top three, so additional rounds would not reorder them.

history.rationale: Arg157 is a highly conserved catalytic-domain residue implicated in FAD/substrate binding; R157Q is a documented severe MTHFR deficiency allele with near-abolished activity.
R157W scores lower on AM (0.758) than the new top candidates, and the conservative Q substitution is likely milder than W at the same site, so it drops in rank.
Thr227 lies in the FAD-binding TIM-barrel pocket adjacent to the A222 thermolabile site; T227M is a reported severe deficiency mutation causing drastic loss of activity.
Position-level evidence (T227I AM 0.966, ESM ~0) transfers strongly, and T227M is a documented severe-deficiency allele; kept just below the directly-scored T227I.
Arg183 is conserved in the catalytic barrel and its loss removes a key charge interaction; R183Q is reported in severe MTHFR deficiency patients.
Surface-Arg to Gln is a conservative change with no direct evidence, and it is displaced by five candidates with measured high LOF-proxy scores.

rejection.reason: Surface-Arg to Gln is a conservative change with no direct evidence, and it is displaced by five candidates with measured high LOF-proxy scores.

history.rationale: Arg335 is a conserved catalytic-domain arginine; the R335C substitution is a known severe deficiency allele that destabilizes the enzyme and abolishes activity.
No direct evidence and likely surface/regulatory position; dropped to keep the pool within the 10-candidate cap.

rejection.reason: No direct evidence and likely surface/regulatory position; dropped to keep the pool within the 10-candidate cap.

history.rationale: Arg377 sits at the catalytic/linker interface and R377C is a recurrent severe MTHFR deficiency mutation with strongly reduced specific activity.
Untested linker-region Arg with weaker mechanistic rationale than the newly evidenced core candidates.

rejection.reason: Untested linker-region Arg with weaker mechanistic rationale than the newly evidenced core candidates.

history.rationale: A222 is the FAD-pocket residue whose mild V substitution already causes thermolability; introducing proline should break the local secondary structure and abolish FAD binding.

A222V is only mildly pathogenic (AM 0.632, thermolabile not null), suggesting the position tolerates substitution; the proline variant is retained only as a backbone-breaking hypothesis at lower rank.
Gly149 is a conserved small residue in a tightly packed loop of the catalytic barrel; a bulky charged arginine should sterically disrupt folding of the active site.
Superseded by the directly scored G149V at the same position to avoid redundancy within the candidate cap.

rejection.reason: Superseded by the directly scored G149V at the same position to avoid redundancy within the candidate cap.

history.rationale: Asp223 is adjacent to the FAD-binding A222 region and likely contributes a conserved hydrogen-bond/charge network; D→N would neutralize this contact.
Very conservative Asp→Asn in a locally tolerant segment (A222V only mildly pathogenic); unlikely to abolish activity.

rejection.reason: Very conservative Asp→Asn in a locally tolerant segment (A222V only mildly pathogenic); unlikely to abolish activity.

history.rationale: Trp339 is a buried aromatic in the catalytic domain core; replacement by arginine buries a charge and should unfold/inactivate the enzyme.
Analogous Trp→Arg burial logic performed extremely well at W421; retained as an untested candidate to query with the phenotype tool next round.
Leu323 is in a predicted buried helix of the catalytic barrel; proline substitution would break the helix and destabilize the active-site scaffold.
Helix-breaking proline in the catalytic domain remains a plausible null allele but is untested; retained at low rank pending direct scoring.
